title: Starter acne routine for blackheads, whiteheads and pimples
steps: Wash the face twice a day with a benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid acne wash
For whiteheads and blackheads, apply an over-the-counter adapalene (retinoid) gel to unclog pores
Do not scrub blackheads; scrubbing can make acne worse
Leave pimples alone; do not pop pus-filled bumps
Give the routine 6 to 8 weeks before judging results
notes: A common starting point for mild blackheads, whiteheads and small pimples. The AAD advises seeing a dermatologist if acne has not improved after 6 to 8 weeks, or right away for deep nodules or cysts, which can scar.
sourceTitle: How to treat different types of acne

title: Gentle daily habits for acne-prone skin
steps: Wash up to twice a day and after sweating, using a mild, non-abrasive cleanser and fingertips (not a washcloth or sponge)
Choose gentle, alcohol-free products; skip astringents, toners and exfoliants
Keep oily hair off the forehead and wash it more often
Stick with one treatment for several weeks to a few months instead of switching often
Daytime: broad-spectrum, water-resistant SPF 30+ sunscreen labeled non-comedogenic, since some acne treatments increase sun sensitivity
notes: Everyday care that supports any acne treatment. Picking or popping raises the risk of scars and dark spots; the AAD suggests a board-certified dermatologist if breakouts continue despite these steps.

title: Everyday sunscreen routine
steps: Pick a broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher
Apply about 15 minutes before going outdoors
Use about 1 ounce (a shot glass) for exposed body skin and at least 1 teaspoon for the face
Cover often-missed spots: neck, ears, tops of feet, legs, and the scalp if hair is thinning (or wear a wide-brimmed hat)
Use a lip balm with SPF 30 or higher
Reapply every 2 hours and right after swimming or sweating
notes: For everyone, year-round, since UV reaches skin on cloudy days and in winter. A tinted sunscreen with iron oxide may also help guard against dark spots.

title: Athlete's foot routine: twice daily
steps: Wash feet twice a day and gently towel-dry between the toes
Apply an OTC antifungal cream, spray or powder (such as terbinafine, miconazole, clotrimazole or tolnaftate) twice a day
Keep using it until a week after the rash clears; results can take 2 to 4 weeks
Change socks at least daily, wear breathable shoes and rotate pairs so they dry
Wear waterproof sandals in pools, showers and locker rooms, and don't share shoes
notes: For mild athlete's foot. If OTC products don't work or the infection seems more serious, a doctor may confirm the diagnosis and prescribe stronger treatment, since athlete's foot can resemble dry skin or dermatitis.

title: Jock itch and ringworm routine
steps: Ringworm on the skin: apply an OTC antifungal cream or ointment, usually twice a day for 2 to 4 weeks
Jock itch: apply an OTC antifungal cream, spray or powder twice a day for 10 to 14 days
For itch, hold a cool, wet washcloth on the area for 20 to 30 minutes, 2 to 6 times a day, using a clean cloth each time
Finish the full course as directed, even after the rash looks better
Wash used washcloths in hot, sudsy water
notes: For small, mild fungal rashes on the body or groin. The AAD advises a dermatologist if jock itch doesn't clear with home care, ringworm covers a large area, or it is on the scalp, beard or nails, which need prescription medicine.

title: Simple dandruff shampoo routine
steps: Choose a dandruff shampoo with zinc pyrithione, salicylic acid, sulfur, selenium sulfide, ketoconazole or coal tar
Lather onto the scalp; some formulas work best left on 5 to 10 minutes before rinsing (follow the label)
Fine, straight or oily hair: wash often and use the dandruff shampoo about twice a week
Coarse, curly or coily hair: use it about once a week on the scalp only, then usual hair products
If one shampoo stops helping, alternate with one that has a different active ingredient
notes: For common flaking and itchy scalp. Coal tar can make the scalp more sun-sensitive; see a dermatologist if dandruff persists or is severe, as it may be seborrheic dermatitis, psoriasis or a fungal infection.

title: Quick itch-relief routine
steps: Try not to scratch; it can irritate skin and worsen the itch
Hold a cool, damp washcloth on the itchy area for about 5 to 10 minutes
Soak in a warm colloidal oatmeal bath
Moisturize with a fragrance-free product while skin is still damp, and whenever it itches
If that's not enough, try a cooling menthol or calamine product, or an OTC pramoxine cream or gel (refrigerating adds to the cooling)
Wear loose cotton clothing and avoid big temperature swings
notes: For everyday itch from dryness or minor irritation. The AAD suggests a dermatologist if the itch doesn't improve or the skin changes (redness, swelling, rash, bumps or sores).
sourceTitle: Stop itchy skin in its tracks

title: Poison ivy rash care at home
steps: Right away, wash skin with warm soapy water, rubbing alcohol or dish soap to remove the plant oil
Wearing gloves, remove and machine-wash clothing and wash tools, leashes and pet fur
Don't scratch and leave blisters intact
Ease itch with cool, damp washcloths, calamine lotion, or hydrocortisone cream for mild cases
Take short cool showers or short warm baths with colloidal oatmeal or baking soda
Oral antihistamine pills may help; avoid antihistamine creams on the skin, which can worsen the rash
notes: Only for mild rashes on small areas when the cause is clearly poison ivy, oak or sumac. Seek emergency care for trouble breathing or swallowing, swelling of the face, or a rash near the eyes, mouth or genitals or over most of the body.
sourceTitle: Poison ivy, oak, and sumac: How to treat the rash

title: Dry skin routine: bath, seal, protect
steps: Keep showers or baths to 5 to 10 minutes in warm (not hot) water
Use a gentle, fragrance-free cleanser sparingly, only where needed, and pat dry
Apply a fragrance-free cream or ointment right away while skin is damp; look for glycerin, petrolatum, shea butter or lanolin
Reapply moisturizer several times a day and use petroleum jelly or lip balm on lips
Run a humidifier and wear gloves for wet chores and cold weather
notes: For everyday dry, rough skin. Products with alcohol, fragrance or retinoids can worsen dryness; persistent dryness may signal eczema, psoriasis or another condition worth a dermatologist visit.
sourceTitle: Dermatologists' top tips for relieving dry skin

title: Eczema-friendly daily skin care
steps: Bathe or shower for 5 to 10 minutes in warm water
While skin is still damp, apply a fragrance-free cream or ointment (not a lotion)
Moisturize again whenever skin feels dry
Choose products labeled fragrance-free rather than unscented, and patch-test new ones on the inner arm daily for 7 to 10 days
Wear loose cotton clothing and wash new clothes in fragrance- and dye-free detergent before wearing
notes: A common at-home routine for people with eczema (atopic dermatitis). It works alongside a dermatologist's plan; the AAD suggests telling your dermatologist which steps help so treatment can be adjusted.
sourceTitle: How to treat eczema at home

title: Excessive sweating routine: night and morning
steps: Use an antiperspirant (it reduces sweat), not just a deodorant (it only masks odor)
Night: apply antiperspirant to dry skin at bedtime
Morning: apply again
Use it anywhere heavy sweating happens, such as palms, back or behind the knees
For sweaty feet: cotton or moisture-wicking socks, leather shoes, and don't wear the same pair two days in a row
notes: For people bothered by heavy sweating. There is no cure for hyperhidrosis, but if sweating persists despite these steps a board-certified dermatologist can build a treatment plan.

title: Hereditary hair thinning: a starter routine
steps: Apply minoxidil to a dry scalp on the thinning area, as often as the label directs, and wash your hands afterward
Wash with a shampoo made for your hair type and use conditioner after every shampoo
Let hair air-dry when you can, and keep blow dryers and flat irons on low heat
Avoid tight ponytails, braids and buns, which pull on the hair
Give minoxidil about 4 months before judging results; some extra shedding at first is common
notes: For gradual, hereditary thinning. Sudden, patchy or clumped hair loss, or loss with a sore or scaly scalp, needs a board-certified dermatologist rather than an OTC trial.

title: Fading dark spots: a patient routine
steps: First stop whatever is causing the spots where possible (for example, treating acne or avoiding irritating products)
Every morning, use a tinted broad-spectrum, water-resistant SPF 30+ sunscreen with iron oxide; reapply every 2 hours and after sweating
Add one OTC ingredient such as azelaic acid, glycolic acid, kojic acid, vitamin C or a retinoid like adapalene gel
Stick to gentle, fragrance-free products and stop anything that burns or stings
Expect slow change: spots a few shades darker often take 6 to 12 months to fade
notes: For dark spots and uneven tone, including in darker skin tones. Avoid imported products that may contain hidden steroids or mercury; see a dermatologist if OTC options don't help, since prescription-strength treatment may be needed.
sourceTitle: How to fade dark spots in darker skin tones
